description: Ego-policy swap experiment over scenarios/local/benchmark, run on the bundled local simulator (--backend pygame) instead of CARLA. Each scenario is run twice: once as compiled (the ego driven by its behaviour-tree timeline) and once with the ego's actuation handed to the IDM policy through the --ego-policy entry point. Everything else -- NPC timelines, events, monitors, spawn geometry -- is identical between the two arms, exactly as in benchmark.json.
relationship_to_benchmark_json: These are ports, not the same runs. The .osc files stage the same four natural-language scenarios at the centre junction (80, 80) of the synthesised `grid` town rather than at Town10HD_Opt junctions 189/841/134. Absolute numbers are therefore not comparable with benchmark.json; the intended OUTCOME per scenario is, and that is what expect_collision encodes. See the header comment of each .osc for the per-scenario differences.

idm_parameters.note: Library defaults, identical across all four scenarios, so the arm differs only in the controller and not in per-scenario tuning.

scenarios.name: red_light
scenarios.intent: A vehicle running the crossing red T-bones the ego inside the junction.

scenarios.name: right_turn
scenarios.intent: A vehicle already on the lane the ego turns onto rear-ends it.

scenarios.name: left_turn
scenarios.intent: An oncoming vehicle strikes the ego mid unprotected-left-turn.

scenarios.name: stop_sign
scenarios.intent: The ego negotiates an unsignalised crossing by precedence and nothing is hit.

junction_turn_note: drive() follows waypoint.next()[0], so which way a vehicle goes through a junction is a property of the lane it is on. --junction-turn sets the map-wide preference and the town's lane-pairing rule supplies the per-actor difference: a left turn is connected only from the innermost lane and a right turn only between outermost lanes, so a vehicle on the other lane has no such connector and goes straight. Each scenario's header comment states which actor is on which lane and why.
construct_vocabulary: These scenarios use only constructs the paper documents -- Table 2's capability checklist and Listings 1-3 of the hello_world case study. ram(target:) has been removed: it appears nowhere in the paper, and every adversarial outcome here previously depended on it. The striking vehicle now keeps executing drive() on its own lane at its own declared speed; drive() has no car-following, yielding or collision-avoidance term, so not changing what you are doing IS failing to give way. See PIPELINE_WALKTHROUGH.md, 'Construct provenance'.
impulse_note: Peak impulses are lower than the CARLA benchmark's and lower than this suite's own earlier ram-based runs. ram applied full throttle regardless of the declared speed; without it the declared speed is the actual speed, so left_turn falls from ~19500 to ~5900 and right_turn from ~12400 to ~4300. collision_occurred and the intended partner are unchanged, and those are what expect_collision and intended_partner test.
